ANSWER: The brain gives no stated source for why the computer kept going. The only explanation is an agent's own inference, not a documented fact: an agent concluded that the software's priority scheduling is why the computer kept flying through the Apollo 11 alarms (src: agent, 2026-10-24). This software was written by Margaret Hamilton's team at the MIT Instrumentation Laboratory. The stated facts are these: the Apollo Guidance Computer raised five program alarms (1201/1202) during the powered descent. The first came about 5 minutes after descent initiation. Section 5.3 (pages 5-4 to 5-6) of the mission report records the alarms but gives no cause.
